It does not establish that this PR is implemented. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Agent runs launch commands and tool servers whose resources can outlive their returned output. Cleanup owners report whether those resources closed, controlling state release and whether subsequent work may proceed. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Agent or CLI invocation] --> B[Commands and tool servers] B --> C[Returned output] B --> D[Resource cleanup owners] D --> E{Closure confirmed?} E -->|Yes| F[Release owned state] E -->|No| G[Retain state and refuse replacement] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Previously successful one-shot commands can report cleanup failure and retain state or locks; failed CLI or Gateway cleanup can prevent subsequent owned work. The PR body explicitly accepts this behavior. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Native Windows execution and the installed fresh/existing-state matrix remain deferred; the inspected boundary tests do not establish those deployment outcomes. - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge.
